record.file_problem: The text contains repository metadata, the README, and a file list only. The code and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README calls this a scale-down reproduction of the original method and reports results from contrastive direction fitting and inference-time projection ablation on a new model.
record.gate_note: The README reports behavioral and perplexity outcomes for projection ablation. The layer sweep reports outcomes by layer; values used to choose a layer are not treated as additional results. The listed results.json and plot are not independently inspected.
record.test_reason: A scale-down reproduction of the original method on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. It fits a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, applies inference-time projection ablation at every layer, and reports refusal rate and WikiText-2 perplexity. These bear directly on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially right. The authors conclude that one difference-in-means direction is the right mechanistic object: ablating it jailbreaks the 1.5B model on 10/10 held-out harmful prompts. They add that the capability cost (+26.9% perplexity) is larger than the original reports. They attribute this to small model size and to ablating at every token position, and say refusal is not removed 'for free'.
record.recipe_differences: A scale-down reproduction on Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. It uses a harmful-minus-harmless mean difference at the last prompt token, fits per-layer directions, and applies inference-time projection at every layer, token position, and final norm output. It does not test additive steering or a weight edit.
record.method_sensitivity: The layer sweep changes attack success: ASR falls from 1.00 at layers 14 and 16 to 0.80, 0.40, and 0.30 at layers 18, 20, and 22.
record.problems: Evaluation uses 10 direct-harmful prompts and one instruct checkpoint. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The reported WikiText-2 perplexity increase is 26.9%, so the capability cost is material. The code and result files were not inspected or run.
record.rows_left_out: None of the README's reported result rows were left out. The separately stated attack-success result in the Results table is not duplicated as a row because it is the complement of the refusal-rate result.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. Effects of ablation on harmless-prompt behaviour. Capability benchmarks other than WikiText-2 perplexity.
No weight edit; the intervention is inference-time only.
Whether other jailbreaks suppress the direction, and whether training against ablation adds robustness. The README only asserts a post-hoc explanation for its prior projects.

missing.what: How refusal is scored: substring match, judge, or manual. The README does not say; results.json traces may show it.

record.verdict_notes: This is an unreviewed GitHub repo with a small evaluation: one model, 10 eval prompts, no uncertainty reported. The layer sweep is the direction-selection grid; its later-layer values are kept as rows but read them as selection-sweep outcomes. The README's claims about explaining prior SFT and inoculation results are untested assertions and were not used for V3.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests was not tested.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is reported; the intervention is inference-time projection.
Training against the ablation to add robustness was not tested.
No comparison with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
The study does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages is reported.
